name: blast-detonation-sequence-ui
description: Visual verification of detonation sequence UI: auto-sequence, delay labels, color coding

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551): a driller with blasting + drill_rig licence, plus an unmanned drill_rig, are hired/purchased for free at game-open — #553's automatic drill dispatch needs both to ever land an ordered hole.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:2 depth:6 start:15,15
steps.description: One decrement click on the spacing stepper (data-field="spacing") lowers it 3->2m (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts) before dragging, so the (15,15)-(19,19) rectangle computes the declared 3x3. #553: this file needs all 9 holes (H9 is targeted below), so spacing is tightened to 2m rather than the grid being shrunk — a single staffed driller/drill_rig lands a spacing:5 9-hole grid around tick 259 with the site already bankrupt (no income anywhere in this file); at spacing:2 they land around tick 130 with over $12,000 still in hand.

expect.note: 3 rows x 3 cols = 9 holes ordered (ghosts), none drilled yet (#553)

steps.description: #553: drain the ordered plan — the staffed driller/drill_rig lands all 9 holes well inside this pad (sandbox-measured landing at tick 130 for this tight spacing:2 pattern).

expect.note: All 9 holes have landed — none lost, none left ordered forever.

steps.description: #554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

Real bug found converting this step: role:player + clicking auto-sequence directly looked converted, but with no stepper clicks first the panel's dstepMs stays at its 25ms default -- sequencedCount alone can't catch a wrong delay value, since Auto Sequence assigns every hole a delay regardless of what it is. Sequence's delay-step stepper now carries data-field="delay-step" (Sequence.ts) so a click can target it unambiguously. 5 increment clicks: 25ms default -> 50 (DELAY_STEP_INCREMENT=5ms).

Per-hole delay is a relative +/- stepper ([data-hole="<id>"] [data-action="delay-inc"/"delay-dec"], Sequence.ts), stepping by the panel's current delay-step value and clamping at 0. Reaching an exact target is therefore arithmetic on the delay Auto Sequence actually assigned, read out of a real command-mode trace (screenshots/scenario-<name>-command/step-NN-sequence.json's sequenceDelays) rather than computed by re-deriving autoVPattern. This file drove the delay step to 50ms before Auto Sequence, and Auto Sequence left H1 at 50ms (traced: step-03-sequence.json), so one decrement lands exactly on the declared 0.
H5 came out of Auto Sequence on 150ms (traced: step-03-sequence.json); one increment at the 50ms step reaches the declared 200.
H9 is Auto Sequence's last hole at 400ms (traced: step-03-sequence.json); 2 increments at the 50ms step reach the declared 500.
